setlist.title: Going Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Hard To Handle** (2 reviews): Hard To Handle is very nice, with an excellent jam that holds together; Hard To Handle is singled out as awesome, with palpable energy [4][12]
- **Yellow Dog Story** (1 review): Bobby's Yellow Dog Story had the reviewer laughing [4]
- **Me And Bobby McGee** (1 review): Reviewer believes the high harmony on Bobby McGee at times is Jerry [6]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Jerry's playing on China Cat is excellent and teasingly light [4]
- **Me And My Uncle** (1 review): Reviewer rates this among the best Me and My Uncle versions the band played before 1975 [2]

## Setlist highlights

- **Yellow Dog Story**: back after 114 archived shows (514 days) [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-08-04.sbd.miller.95308.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 131 min; rated 3.89/5 by 27 [1]. Said about its sound: Many tracks suffer distortion, though the reviewer says the show still has a sweet vibe; Phil's bass is mixed up front, and the rest of the band still plays well; Front-of-house mix with a rough start; it takes three or four songs before the sound settles [2][3][5][9][11][12]

## Around the show

- The show was played at the prison that held Augie Stanley, known as Bear, the band's sound mentor [3]
- Reviewer thinks Donna sings the high harmonies on some of the early songs [6]
- The set includes five Pigpen songs [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-08-04.sbd.miller.95308.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD [1]. Also: Reviewer says some of this show has already been released on Road Trips [8]
